title: The House
description: Casa Meyer, the last house designed by Luis Barragán, 1978.

blocks.html: Casa Meyer is the last house Luis Barragán designed. He drew it in October 1978, at seventy-six, for his friend Barbara Meyer, on a hillside street in Bosques de las Lomas on the western edge of Mexico City. It remains a private home.

image.alt: The street facade of Casa Meyer: a long white wall with a yellow sliding gate under a hedge of vines and bougainvillea
image.caption: The street facade, with the yellow gate closed.

blocks.html:
From the street the house is a single low wall. A thin concrete lintel runs its full length and carries a hedge of vines, bougainvillea and trumpet flowers that has grown over the wall for decades. Beneath the lintel there are two openings: a narrow white door for people and the wide yellow gate for cars. The gate slides rather than swings, so the wall is never broken.

The yellow is the warm chrome yellow Barragán used in the corridor of Casa Gilardi two years earlier. It is the only colour on the street.

image.alt: Watercolor of the street facade with the yellow gate
image.caption: Watercolor study of the street facade.

image.alt: Pencil elevation drawing titled Fachada Sur, dated 31 October 1978, dedicated to Baby Meyer de Garate
image.caption: Fachada Sur, 31 October 1978.

blocks.html:
Two elevation drawings survive in Barragán's own hand, both dated 31 October 1978 and both dedicated across the bottom: para Baby Meyer de Garate, con todo cariño. They show a house of stacked, nearly windowless volumes, a tall chimney wall, and a flight of steps running along the garden side. The openings are filled solid black; the sunlit and shaded planes are shaded in pencil.

[The house today: who lives there, what has been kept, what has changed, and why it is being opened to visitors. To be written with the family.]
